title: Gideon and the Inheritance
premise: Astrid Reyes, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has quietly unraveled three 'accidents' the police closed, is pulled into the strangest case of her career when the coffin of Harlan Gideon—founder of the town that bears his name—is exhumed and found empty. Following a ledger hidden in plain sight among the town's monuments and deeds, she uncovers a century-old scheme in which Gideon faked his own death to escape his partners, who have kept the town running on his stolen fortune ever since. As the descendants of those partners close ranks around her, Astrid must decide whether exposing the truth will save the town or destroy it. In the end, she finds Gideon's living heir hiding in plain sight and forces a public reckoning—not through the courts, but by making the whole town remember what it chose to forget.
about_author: Isandro Dunmore is the pen name of a former claims adjuster turned novelist who spent a decade reading other people's disasters for a living. He writes mysteries about paper trails, small towns, and the lies communities agree to keep.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. Opening her fourth suspicious file—the exhumation order for Harlan Gideon—Astrid recalls, in perfect detail, the three deaths she solved alone and why she never told anyone. Emotional beat: wary competence masking loneliness; she likes being invisible, and this case threatens that.

chapters.title: An Empty Box
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. At the cemetery, she witnesses the exhumation: Gideon's coffin holds only river stones and a brass token stamped with a ledger number. The town council watches her like hawks. Emotional beat: cold dread—the town isn't shocked; it's guarding something.

chapters.title: The Gideon Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. Using her memory of town records, Astrid realizes the brass token matches entries in property deeds filed the week Gideon 'died'—a ledger hidden across a century of paperwork. Someone ransacks her office that night. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into fear; she's no longer invisible.

chapters.title: Descendants
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. She interviews the four founding families' heirs, each charming, each lying in ways only she can see—a twitch, a rehearsed phrase repeated verbatim from decades-old testimony. Emotional beat: quiet triumph turning to isolation as she realizes everyone knows more than she does.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. A retired archivist tells her Gideon drowned—or was said to—and hands her a water-damaged photograph of five partners, one face scratched out. Cross-referencing, Astrid identifies the fifth man: still alive, still local, under another name. Emotional beat: grief for the archivist, who is found dead two days later.

chapters.title: The Fourth Accident
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. The archivist's death is ruled a fall. Astrid, furious, reconstructs the scene from memory and proves it was staged—but planting her evidence means going to the police she's always avoided. Emotional beat: rage and resolve; invisibility now feels like complicity.

chapters.title: Ledger Complete
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. Decoding the full ledger, Astrid learns Gideon embezzled from his partners first—they discovered him, he staged his death, and they've been laundering his fortune through the town ever since, paying for its silence with its prosperity. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; the villain and the benefactor are the same man.

chapters.title: Cornered
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. The heirs offer her money, then threats; her apartment burns with all her files inside. But her memory needs no files. They realize it too late, and the hunt turns physical. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into clarity—she stops running and starts planning.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Buried
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. Climax. Astrid traces the ledger's final entry to a nursing home where the scratched-out partner—Gideon himself, ninety-four and unrepentant—has lived under a false name for decades. Confronted, he offers her a place in the arrangement. She refuses and records everything. Emotional beat: icy confrontation; temptation answered with principle.

chapters.title: Remembered
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. Resolution. At the founders' day ceremony, Astrid publicly reads the ledger aloud, forcing the heirs to confess rather than let Gideon's confession air. The town reels, loses its myth, and begins, painfully, to tell the truth. Astrid, finally seen, accepts it. Emotional beat: bittersweet justice—truth costs the town its comfort and gives Astrid her name back.
